kpis.label: Reality Coverage
kpis.help: Share of monitored property facts and attributes reflected in AI answers (from published Reality Gap).

executiveAssessment.text: Executive Conclusion — The St. Regis Mexico City's priority is a Reality Gap in how a distinctive part of the proposition is represented in AI answers. Why this is the primary issue — Urban Luxury is recognized in only 0.9% of monitored answers. That is low enough to matter commercially if the attribute is part of how the hotel should win relevant traveler needs. Overall scores can hide this concentrated representation miss. Broader Scenario Presence (100%) and Consideration (85.7%) do not, by themselves, prove the distinctive attribute is traveling into answers. If distinctive property attributes are weakly represented, the hotel can look broadly visible while still losing the moments where its real proposition should matter. This is a representation problem first, not automatically a peer-competition program. Where the pattern is concentrated — Scenario Capture is softest in Business Travel (100.0%) versus stronger Adventure (100.0%). These are current-period scenario-capture rates from demandCapture.byIntent — not answer-level consideration. Reality Coverage is 53.8% (7 of 13 monitored attributes recognized). High-severity gaps include Urban Luxury; Five Diamond Positioning. What management should focus on — Focus first on Urban Luxury. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it. What not to overreact to — No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet. This period can be evaluated on its own; change over time is not shown. Independent Positioning shows #1 of 6 with Portfolio AI Presence 85.7%. Portfolio and Core metrics share observation context but are not interchangeable denominators. What to watch next — Open Reality Gap evidence for Urban Luxury and compare recognition cues with official property pages and high-authority travel sources. Then check a small set of related demand scenarios for whether the attribute appears when competitors are named. Anchored metrics (current published ADP): AI Consideration 85.7%; Scenario Presence 100.0%; Reality Coverage 53.8%. Biggest Strength (platform): Often placed near the top when AI ranks hotels. Biggest Constraint (platform): No single dominant weakness.

actionAgenda.actionTitle: Stand up a TripAdvisor management-response program with owner, SLA, and theme tracking — focus: designate accountable owner, set response SLA, identify recurring complaint themes monthly
actionAgenda.observedIssue: TripAdvisor appears in 64.1% of cited sources in the current monitoring period (41 citations), making response quality and factual corrections operationally material when misconceptions appear.
actionAgenda.recommendedAction: Confirm the hotel’s canonical facts for TripAdvisor responses with the accountable owner (The St. Regis Mexico City). Complete the applicable checklist items: designate accountable owner; set response SLA (property-configured; do not invent a default unless governed); identify recurring complaint themes monthly; correct factual misconceptions where appropriate; track response rate. Audit each target source and record current wording/state: TripAdvisor. Correct only the sources where facts are missing, conflicting, or outdated. Do not change measurement methodology. Store completion evidence (canonical policy summary, sources reviewed, sources corrected, URLs/screenshots, completion date). Notify Dealality of completion so the next monitoring period can check the expected signal without assuming causation.
actionAgenda.rationale: This action addresses an observed information/positioning gap in the current monitoring period. It does not claim a guaranteed metric uplift.
actionAgenda.expectedSignal: Dealality will monitor whether tripadvisor responses recognition and related scenario inclusion change in the next monitoring period. Monitoring alone does not establish causation.
